about.heading: About WIC
about.intro: WIC is a federally-funded health and nutrition program for women, infants, and children. WIC helps families by providing checks for buying healthy supplemental foods from WIC-authorized vendors, nutrition education, and help finding healthcare and other community services. In California, 84 WIC agencies provide services locally to over 1.45 million participants each month at over 650 sites throughout the State.
about.who.heading: Who Is WIC For?
about.who.women: Women who are pregnant, breastfeeding, or just had a baby.
about.who.children: Children under 5 years old (including foster children)
about.who.income: Families with low to medium income (working families may qualify)
about.who.quizPrompt: To see if you qualify for WIC, try our 'Do I Qualify?' quiz.
about.start.heading: Getting Started with WIC
about.start.body: Call 1-888-WIC-WORKS to talk to a WIC staff member who can help you find your local WIC office. Check out California's official WIC site for more official information about WIC. Watch the video below for an introduction to the program.
about.resources.heading: Resources
about.resources.intro: WIC offers lots of programs and services to help keep California healthy. From educational materials to programs that help participants shop at local farmers' markets, WIC can help make sure you and your kids get the nutrition you need.
about.markets.heading: Farmers' markets
about.markets.intro: WIC offers two programs to help you buy fruits and vegetables at your local farmers' market.
about.markets.fmnp.heading: Farmers' Market Nutrition Program (FMNP)
about.markets.fmnp.body: The Farmers' Market Nutrition Program (FMNP) is funded by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) to provide fresh, nutritious, locally grown fruits and vegetables from farmers' markets to WIC families and seniors. Each eligible WIC family or senior receives {amount} in checks each season to purchase fresh fruits, vegetables, and cut herbs from a WIC authorized farmer at WIC authorized market in California.
about.markets.fvc.heading: WIC Fruit & Vegetable Checks (FVC)
about.markets.fvc.body: In October 2009, fruit and vegetables were added to the WIC food package for participants to purchase at authorized grocery stores. In May 2010 the first farmers' market was authorized to accept WIC fruit and vegetable checks. Since 2010, over 200 farmers and 35 markets have been authorized to accept the fruit and vegetable checks.
about.education.heading: Educational Materials
about.education.body: The more you know about health, the easier it is to keep your kids healthy. Check out the official WIC site's education materials for more.
about.wicit.heading: About WICit
about.wicit.body: WICit and findwic.com are not affiliated with any federal or state WIC programs. WICit was created by Code for Sacramento to help Californians more easily get and use WIC. If you're interested in deploying WICit in your state, check out the WICit github repo.

qualify.heading: Do I qualify for WIC?
qualify.stepMissing: That step doesn't exist. Start the quiz over.
qualify.residency.intro: This short survey is designed to help you figure out if you qualify for WIC. Your answers are not saved, this is just for you to figure out if you qualify for WIC.
qualify.residency.warning: Please keep in mind, this is just a guide. Only local WIC Agency staff can determine for certain if you qualify for WIC services. Call 1-888-WIC-WORKS to find out for sure if you qualify.
qualify.residency.question: Do you live in California?
qualify.category.breastfeeding: Are you breastfeeding a child that is less than one year-old?
qualify.category.infant: Do you have a child that is less than six months-old?
qualify.category.child: Do you have a child that is less than five years-old?
qualify.category.otherPrograms: Do you currently receive any of the following:
qualify.income.familySize: How many people (including unborn children) in your family?
qualify.income.combined: What is your family's combined income?
qualify.income.missingFamilySize: Please enter the number of people in your family.
qualify.result.success.heading: You probably qualify for WIC!
qualify.result.success.body: Your next step is to talk to a WIC agent. Call 1-888-WIC-WORKS to get started.
qualify.result.residency.heading: Sorry, you have to live in-state to qualify for WIC in California.
qualify.result.residency.body: If you're moving here, WIC can work with you. Give them a call at 1-888-WIC-WORKS.
qualify.result.category.heading: Sorry, WIC is for people who identify with one of the following:
qualify.result.category.body: A WIC agent may be able to help you find a different program that can help. To talk to a WIC agent, call 1-888-WIC-WORKS.
qualify.result.income.heading: You might not qualify for WIC.
qualify.result.income.body: WIC is for families making less than 185% of the Federal Poverty Level ({threshold} for a family of four in {year}). You should still talk to a WIC agent at 1-888-WIC-WORKS to find out for sure whether you qualify.
qualify.result.unknown.heading: Whoops!
qualify.result.unknown.body: Told you we don't save your data! You can take the quiz again though.
